question:
Three weeks after undergoing a loop electrosurgical excision procedure for cervical dysplasia, a
19-year-old woman visits her physician for a follow-up evaluation. Pathology results confirm cervical
intraepithelial neoplasia II (CIN II) with clear surgical margins. Her medical history is unremarkable, and
she reports feeling well. She lives with her boyfriend and is planning to conceive soon. Vital signs are
normal. Pelvic examination reveals a normal vulva and vagina, while speculum examination shows
cicatrized tissue on the cervix. What is the most appropriate health maintenance recommendation for
this patient at this time? Answer Choices: (A) HPV testing in 6 months (B) Annual Pap smear until 3
consecutive normal results are obtained (C) HPV vaccination to prevent recurrence (D) Cervical
cytology in 3 years (E) Pap smear and HPV testing in 1 year (F) Immediate hysterectomy due to CIN II
(G) Pap smear and HPV testing in 5 years (H) Colposcopy and biopsies in 6 months (I) Colposcopy
and endocervical curettage in 12 months (J) Repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure in 6
months
 A. Cervical cytology in 3 years
B. HPV vaccination to prevent recurrence
C. Immediate hysterectomy due to CIN II
D. Pap smear and HPV testing in 1 year
E. Pap smear and HPV testing in 5 years
F. HPV testing in 6 months
G. Annual Pap smear until 3 consecutive normal results are obtained
H. Repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure in 6 months
I. Colposcopy and biopsies in 6 months
J. Colposcopy and endocervical curettage in 12 months
